title: Rotation invariance: a planar scenario turned bodily gives the planar results turned
description: Two planar scenarios (newton-recovers-gm and forecast-envelope, read from the planar vector files) are lifted to 3D, given an out-of-plane pointing error, and fitted in full 3D: flat, turned by a fixed rotation, and turned so that one fix sits on the +z pole. The rotated results are the flat results turned by the rotation; the flat results reproduce the planar vectors in the plane.
units: SI: m, s, m/s, m/s^2, rad. A fix is [azimuth, elevation(, range)] of the inertial direction ship -> target: azimuth = atan2(d_y, d_x) in (-pi, pi], elevation = asin(d_z / |d|). sigma is per component; sigma_az carries the 1 / cos(elevation) of an isotropic pointing error. Attitudes are unit quaternions [w, x, y, z], body to inertial. Accelerometer samples are [f_x, f_y, f_z] in the body frame.
frame: Right-handed inertial. Gauge: body A at the origin and at rest at t = 0 of every attempt (spec 3.4). Body frame: +x forward, +y left, +z up.

propagation.note: Reference setting; all times are multiples of dt. Any propagator whose position error over the arc is below ~1 m reproduces the expected values.

tolerance.numeric: Fits with compare = numeric: |x_impl - x_ref| <= 0.05 sigma_ref per parameter; |sigma_impl / sigma_ref - 1| <= 0.05; |chi2_impl / chi2_ref - 1| <= 0.02; |rho_impl - rho_ref| <= 0.02. Tier L windows: same boundaries (t0, t1, nFixes) and |g_impl - g_ref| <= 0.05 sigma_ref. Profile nodes: |g_impl - g_ref| <= 0.1 sigma_ref.
tolerance.qualitative: Fits with compare = qualitative are grossly misfitted (chi2/nu > 25) or unconverged; only the inequalities in `checks` and any heldOut.pass value are required.
tolerance.physicalClaims: Per check, stated in `checks`. The generator refuses to write a vector whose claims fail.

notes: Expected values: every fit, the Tier L windows and profile, the present state and the forecast points of each case, with the usual tolerances. In addition an implementation should show the two equalities itself: its rotated results against its own flat results turned by `rotation` (tolerance in assumptions-3d.json, rotationInvariance.tolerance.rotatedVsFlat), and its flat results against the planar vector.
The noise scale differs between the planar and the flat run because the flat run has elevation rows; the state term of the forecast is compared after dividing by each run's own noise scale.

`cameraSigma` is null in the forecast cases: the camera misalignment is held fixed in the present-state fit, as in the planar vector. The pole case shows why the bearing residual is formed in the tangent plane at the measured direction (spec 2.1): the azimuth of the fix at the pole is arbitrary and its sigma_az is very large.
`truth` blocks are for checking only and must never reach the estimator (P11). Measurements whose target is not a modelled body are ignored by that fit.
Covariances of positions are [xx, xy, xz, yy, yz, zz].

checks.claim: The rotated scenario is fully three-dimensional (elevations beyond 45 deg) and the pole scenario has a fix within 1 mrad of the +z pole, where azimuth is undefined
checks.label: [DEMONSTRATED: reference generator]

checks.claim: Tier G on the rotated data gives the flat result turned by the rotation: state and its covariance turned, mu.A and the body-frame camera misalignment unchanged, chi2 unchanged (estimates within 0.001 sigma, sigmas within 0.001, chi2 within 1e-06)
checks.label: [DEMONSTRATED: reference generator]

checks.claim: Tier G on the pole data gives the flat result turned by the rotation: state and its covariance turned, mu.A and the body-frame camera misalignment unchanged, chi2 unchanged (estimates within 0.001 sigma, sigmas within 0.001, chi2 within 1e-06)
checks.label: [DEMONSTRATED: reference generator]

checks.claim: The flat 3D fit reproduces the planar vector in the plane: x, y, vx, vy, mu.A and the camera misalignment about z within 0.001 sigma, their sigmas within 0.001, and the chi2 of the azimuth and range rows within 0.0001 of the planar chi2
checks.label: [DEMONSTRATED: reference generator]

checks.claim: The flat fit's z and vz are consistent with zero (within 3 sigma) and the elevation rows add one residual per fix
checks.label: [DEMONSTRATED: reference generator]

checks.claim: Tier L on the rotated data: the same windows (the vector sweep does not depend on the frame) and local scales within 0.001 sigma of the flat ones
checks.label: [DEMONSTRATED: reference generator]

checks.claim: Tier L on the flat data: the planar vector's windows (t0, t1, fix count), local scales within 0.001 sigma and their sigmas within 0.001
checks.label: [DEMONSTRATED: reference generator]

checks.claim: The calibration profile (nodes against distance) is the same for flat, rotated and planar data within 0.01 node sigma: it holds no direction
checks.label: [DEMONSTRATED: reference generator]

checks.claim: The present state and its 6x6 covariance from the rotated data are the flat ones turned by the rotation
checks.label: [DEMONSTRATED: reference generator]

checks.claim: The flat present state (x, y, vx, vy) is the planar vector's within 0.001 sigma, with the same sigmas within 0.001
checks.label: [DEMONSTRATED: reference generator]

checks.claim: Forecast from the rotated data: means and 3x3 covariances are the flat ones turned by the rotation (means within 0.001 of the major sigma, covariance entries within 0.001 of its square) and the horizon ends at the same checkpoints
checks.label: [DEMONSTRATED: reference generator]

checks.claim: Forecast from the flat data: in-plane means within 0.001 of the planar major sigma; the profile, hedge and engine terms and the state term (each divided by its own noise scale) within 0.001 of the planar ones; the horizon ends at the planar checkpoints
checks.label: [DEMONSTRATED: reference generator]
